newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money dips on Central Bank cut.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money dips on Central Bank cut.

text.p: Manila overnight money dipped on Tuesday to an average of 10.46875 from 10.53125 percent after the Central Bank cut its overnight rates by 1/16-percentage points, traders said.
The Central Bank's overnight borrowing rate now stands at 10.4375 percent and lending at 12.9375 percent.
"It was just 1/16 lower. But that's enough to trigger a decline in all tenors," said a foreign bank dealer.
She said banks were expecting a bigger cut of 1/8-percentage points from the Central Bank but it obviously wanted to keep the peso stable.
Rates at the money market moved in a narrow band from 10.5 to 10.46875 percent as volume swelled to 25.256 billion from 21.517 billion pesos.
In the secondary market, quoted rates were also lower in line with the Central Bank's move.
More buyers in the market emerged before a further slide in rates. But they found few sellers, dealers said.
"Sellers are hard to find," a trader said.
According to a Reuter poll of seven banks, bid rates ranged at 10.50/10.60 for three-month bills; 10.675 to 10.80 for six months; and 11.15 to 11.25 for one year.
